text.p: - President Milan Kucan started the second round of talks with representatives of parliamentary parties, but did not manage to come to any agreement on a candidate for prime minister. Kucan should name his candidate by January 3.
- Slovenia's army is moving closer and closer to western standards in knowledge, quality and efficiency, according to Gorazd Vidrih, state secretary at the Ministry of Defence.

- Pharmaceutical producer Krka from the southeastern town of Novo Mesto said it would build another production plant in nearby Sentjernej by the end of the century. Krka said the investment would amount to $10 billion.

- Employers and trade unions said on Tuesday they would sign amendments to the collective agreement on December 23, determining workers' social benefits. The agreement will be valid until the end of May, 1997.

- The Ministry of Economic Relations and Development said on Tuesday that a first increase in electricity prices should come in March next year and not in January as electricity distributors have demanded.
- Experts said that only about 20 to 30 percent of Slovenia's 150,000 farms accepted standards of ecologicaly "clean" farming.
- London Stock Exchange on Tuesday recognised Ljubljana Stock Exchnge as a settled and regular bourse and placed it on the list of recognised markets. Ljubljana bourse was founded in 1988.
- Production in Slovenian ironworks fell by 20 percent compared to the previous year. The group said production fell due to harsh market conditions abroad.
